dedupe_keys.name: nsw epa landfill climate adaptation scenario extreme rainfall landfill gas and odour at a mid north coast facility

description: This NSW EPA case study walks through how a landfill operator can adapt to heavier rainfall under climate change. It follows a hypothetical privately owned landfill on the Mid-North Coast of New South Wales that received odour complaints after heavy rain. The owner's investigation traced the odour to extra landfill gas produced in three ways: rain entering through a damaged cap, a saturated open tipping face, and gas and leachate systems going offline during the storm. A site-wide climate risk assessment used medium and high emissions projections, including about 66 millimetres more rain in a 1-in-100-year 24-hour storm by 2050. The page then lists adaptation options, from updating management plans and preventative maintenance of liners and caps, to backup power for gas and leachate systems, climate-aware design of new cells, checking caps and drainage against Australian Rainfall and Runoff 2019, retrofitting gas capture and daily covering, and it recommends an adaptation pathway with trigger points. The case study is free to read on the NSW EPA website. Coverage is one illustrative site in New South Wales. Caveats: the site is hypothetical, no costs are given, and no licence is stated. Simulation uses: failure modes and adaptation options for landfill performance under extreme rainfall scenarios. Related records: the historic landfills climate risk study for England (case_study-england-historic-landfills-climate-change-pollution-risk) looks at the same hazards for closed sites.

name: NSW EPA landfill climate adaptation scenario: extreme rainfall, landfill gas and odour at a Mid-North Coast facility
outcomes: Identifies three pathways from extreme rainfall to excess landfill gas and odour (compromised cap, saturated tipping face, gas and leachate systems going offline) and a menu of adaptation options: updated plans and manuals, preventative maintenance, redundancy such as backup power, climate-aware cell design, reassessment of caps and drainage against ARR 2019, gas capture retrofits and daily cover; the owner is to build an adaptation pathway with trigger points.
